metaphor: Feedback loop as a conduit for progress
source_quote: the feedback loop was like pretty slow back in Nepal... We had to work for like a very long time to come up with like a viable solution
process_disruption_link: Highlights 'workflow_brittleness' and 'integration_friction.' Slow, linear feedback gating contradicts the rapid, iterative cycles needed for AI model refinement and data validation, severely hampering progress.

source_quote: we were not allowed to store any of those data on our side. So we had to go to... the bank's IT department... use their own protocols
process_disruption_link: Exemplifies 'silo_breakdown' (need for cross-functional access) clashing with 'legacy_inflexibility.' Data-centric AI workflows require fluid access, but are blocked by rigid, siloed legacy security and procedural protocols designed for static reporting, not dynamic model training.

metaphor: Expert intuition as a biased oracle
source_quote: we did introduce a lot of bias from these experts... they're rather making decisions based on their own experiences, right?
process_disruption_link: Directly illustrates 'knowledge_clash' and 'ethical_automation_tension.' The tacit, experience-based knowledge of domain experts (traditional) conflicts with and can inadvertently corrupt the data-centric, empirical foundation of the AI model, introducing ethical risk.

metaphor: Management as an invasive overseer vs. a trust-based facilitator
source_quote: Nepalese manager... don't give you a lot of personal space... ask you, why do you need the holiday?... invasive to our personal life. [US:] if you want like a holiday, you just shoot out a mail... they don't really care about what you're doing.
process_disruption_link: Contrasts management styles affecting 'role_reconfiguration.' The invasive, control-based style stifles the autonomy and creative/exploratory thinking required in AI work. The trust-based US style better supports the shift of managers to ethical/system oversight, freeing technical staff for non-linear problem-solving.

negative_cases_contradicting_disruption.assertion: Planning methodologies are standardized and not culturally dependent.
negative_cases_contradicting_disruption.source_quote: I feel like it's not that different because... there's like a standard for software development... it most depends on the size of the company... rather than the culture, I think.
negative_cases_contradicting_disruption.interpretation: Person 2 contradicts the premise that 'procedural_nonlinearity' (AI loops vs. sequential methods) is a primary cultural or universal friction. He suggests formal project management (e.g., Agile, Waterfall) standards are globally adopted, making the *planning container* similar. The disruption may instead occur *within* those standardized phases (e.g., during the 'development' sprint) due to the nature of AI tasks, not the phase-gated structure itself.

negative_cases_contradicting_disruption.assertion: Technical management challenges are universal, not cultural.
negative_cases_contradicting_disruption.source_quote: a lot of people in tech, they don't have experience with management, right? I think it's true for both... Western and eastern... I don't think it's got to do anything with the culture background of the manager. I think it's how technical people are wired to think.
negative_cases_contradicting_disruption.interpretation: Downplays 'cultural_resistance' and 'role_transition_hurdles' as uniquely cultural issues. Positions the core friction as a universal socio-technical transition challenge: technically-expert individuals (common in AI teams) struggling to adopt the human-centric, facilitative management style required for hybrid teams, regardless of national culture.
